items.summary: Axiomatization of physics through probability, mechanics and classical limiting processes. One open problem of the particle-to-continuum programme is an active reward target. The reviewed Lean package also specifies selected kinetic, fluid, elastic and rigid-body models.
scope: The package includes probability consistency, Newtonian mechanics, kinetic-to-fluid limits and elasticity-to-rigid-body limits for explicitly chosen models.
The gas formulations include ensemble and initial-data variants. Their relation to the cited physical models remains part of the stated scope.

Hilbert’s unrestricted physical-sciences programme extends beyond this selected collection. Fable 5.2 accepted the precise specifications under their declared interpretations after four review rounds.

One statement carries a reward: point charges under the untruncated repulsive Coulomb force, started from independent samples of a smooth density, have empirical averages converging to the solution of the three-dimensional Vlasov–Poisson equation. It is open and expected to be true.

That statement is a modern instance of the programme of deriving continuum equations from particle dynamics. It is not a question Hilbert posed, and it is separate from the hard-sphere, Boltzmann and fluid derivations in the selected models.
items.proof_status: The specification and its supporting lemmas compile. The classical-limit obligations remain statements to establish, including known-theorem obligations under the declared hypotheses.

sources.description: The combined obligation for the chosen classical limiting processes.
The active reward target: the known existence theorem together with the open mean-field convergence.
sources.lean:
def VlasovPoissonMeanFieldLimit : Prop :=
  ∀ f₀ : Phase → ℝ, SmoothDensity f₀ →
    (∃ f : ℝ → Phase → ℝ, IsVlasovPoissonSolution f ∧ ∀ z, f 0 z = f₀ z) ∧
    ∀ f : ℝ → Phase → ℝ, IsVlasovPoissonSolution f → (∀ z, f 0 z = f₀ z) →
      ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t →
        ∀ φ : Phase → ℝ, Continuous φ → HasCompactSupport φ →
          ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ →
            Tendsto (fun N => productLaw N f₀ (deviationSet N f t δ φ)) atTop (𝓝 0)

items.summary: Construct the ray class fields of every number field from special values of analytic functions. One recipe for each field must work at every modulus, recover the Artin action on its values, and agree with the classical constructions over the rationals and imaginary quadratic fields.
scope: For every modulus, the special values must generate exactly its ray class field. Acting on a special point by an ideal must agree with acting on its value by the corresponding Artin automorphism.
The same ray fields must classify abelian extensions by degree, Galois group and relative discriminant, with exact finite catalogues and the conductor–discriminant formula.

Over the rationals, the recipe must recover roots of unity when the real place is included and their real traces when it is omitted. Over imaginary quadratic fields, it must recover the j-invariant and Weber values at nonzero points annihilated by the modulus ideal.
items.proof_status: The combined proposition is open. Lean checks its statement and the implication to the general analytic target. A proposed proof still requires mathematical review of how it obtains the special points, since the arithmetic formulas can encode the desired generators indirectly.

sources.description: Combined analytic construction, arithmetic classification and classical benchmarks.
sources.lean:
def Hilbert12Combined : Prop :=
  ∀ (K : Subfield ℂ) [NumberField K],
    ∃ (R : Recipe) (F : R.Functions) (S : ∀ m : Modulus K, R.Specialization F m),
      Nonempty (ClassFieldTheory K) ∧ ∀ C : ClassFieldTheory K,
        (∀ m, RayValueContract C m (S m)) ∧ Nonempty (ArithmeticClassification C) ∧
        RationalBenchmark C S ∧ ImaginaryQuadraticBenchmark C S

items.summary: Classification of real algebraic curves and surfaces, and the number and arrangement of planar limit cycles. The quintic-surface case is an active reward target. A general uniform-bound proof has been claimed and awaits independent verification.
scope: The reviewed output specifies catalogues, realizability, exhaustion, irredundancy and sharp maxima for nonsingular curves and surfaces, together with affine and projective cycle arrangements.
The uniform-bound proposition quantifies over all real planar polynomial vector fields and requires a finite bound depending only on degree.
OpenAI’s September 24, 2026 manuscript claims this uniform-bound assertion. Exact maxima and complete arrangement classifications remain outside its stated result.
The published Lean companion treats quintic Liénard systems with an exact maximum of two cycles. The general uniform bound has no listed Lean proof in that release.
One open case carries a reward: every nonsingular real quintic surface has at most 23 connected components. The maximum is known only to be 23, 24 or 25, so the statement may be true or false.
The quadratic case, at most four limit cycles in degree two, is stated and reviewed. It is held from the reward pool while an unrefereed claim of that exact result remains unreviewed.
items.proof_status: Reviewed on November 13, 2026. The manuscript claims the uniform bound, and Chen, Xiao and Zhang’s October 23 preprint explicitly calls for independent verification. This review found no published full verification or specific refutation of the general argument.

sources.description: A degree-dependent bound on every finite family of distinct isolated periodic orbits.
sources.lean:
def UniformBound : Prop :=
  ∀ d : ℕ, ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ V : PolynomialVectorField,
    V.DegreeAtMost d →
    ∀ (m : ℕ) (cycles : Fin m → Set Plane),
      Function.Injective cycles →
      (∀ i, IsLimitCycle V (cycles i)) → m ≤ N
